limits: Sixty splits, one untuned tree configuration, integer coding.
Conditions A and B use different evaluation pools, so this compares gains rather than arms within one pool.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI.

C106_and_C107_are_withdrawn.what_they_claimed: the monotone decay of the coarsening gain is specific to linear models; under boosting there was no growth (+0.0150 fully informed against +0.0176 absent, difference +0.0029)
C106_and_C107_are_withdrawn.why_the_earlier_null_arose: R138 and R139 both put drug identity codes into the no-identity arm. On the evaluation rows every one of those codes was the reserved code -1, a dead feature. That is now measured directly: with the grouping alone the tree reaches 0.0984, against the 0.032 that the dead-feature design produced.
C106_and_C107_are_withdrawn.so: the decay is a general property of the setup, not of the model family, and the defect was in my encoding rather than in the trees

what_survives.C105: the claim that the fully-informed redundancy is exact only for linear models. R137 measured +0.0152 for the tree in that very condition and this run reproduces exactly +0.0152, so C105 rests on a clean comparison and stands.
what_survives.C115: pathway beats target under both families, measured with grouping-only features, so it is unaffected
what_survives.C113_C114: pathway over target, ridge rounds, unaffected
what_survives.the_frozen_claim: unaffected: it is a ridge result and always said so

the_lesson.class: a dead feature in one arm silently changes what a flexible model does, and it can manufacture a model-family difference
the_lesson.how_to_avoid: before comparing arms across model families, confirm every feature carries information in the evaluation condition; the check is cheap and I skipped it twice
the_lesson.count: fifth instance of this class in the programme
